messages:
Alex (support): heads up — ACME reported a sudden cost surge + 422 errors from our embeddings endpoint this morning. They say latency also jumped from ~60ms to 600-1200ms for some requests.

Alex (support): sample error they pasted: `422 "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 384"` and some intermittent `502` with `GPU OOM` in the logs. Billing shows a spike in embedding units between 07:05-07:20 UTC.

Maria (observability): thanks — can we get the request id / trace id for a failing request? also want the dashboard snapshot for per-request latency breakdown (queueing vs model vs network). I suspect batching config or a wrong model alias.

Alex (support): sent trace id `trace-0a1b2c3d` and two sample request payloads. attaching curl for reproducibility:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"embed-small-legacy","input":["hello world"]}'
```

Alex (support): customer says they recently rotated to `embed-small-legacy` from `embed-large-v2` and their client lib still sets expected dim=1536.

Priya (support-l2): that explains the dimension mismatch. `embed-small-legacy` outputs 384 vectors. If their ingestion expects 1536, downstream code might be failing and retrying causing duplicate billing. But the latency increase and 502/ GPU OOM suggests some requests were routed to the wrong hardware profile (large model on dedicated GPU).

Chris (eng-runtime): seeing trace-0a1b2c3d in our tracing — the route `embed.vectorize.v1` shows a 900ms total. Breakdown in the trace spans: frontend queue 120ms, router 30ms, batching hold 560ms, model decode 190ms. Batching hold is long because one request had a malformed payload that prevented batching optimization and forced sequential fallback.

Maria (observability): posted link to per-route latency view (console/embed/route/embed.vectorize.v1?range=15m). Key thing: `batching_hold_ms` spike correlates with a client sending single large requests with `Content-Encoding: gzip` missing (we saw `Content-Length` mismatch). That triggers our fallback path where the request is reinterpreted and delayed.

Jordan (billing): billing shows ~4x embed units during the window. There are many short retries from the client (5xx -> retry) — each retry is billable. We should confirm whether retries were client-side. If so, we can offer a one-time invoice credit after root cause.

Priya (support-l2): customer wrote their SDK sets `expected_dim=1536` and hasn't updated to the new model. Suggest asking them to: 1) switch to the correct model alias for 1536 dims (`embed-large-v2`) or 2) update ingestion to accept 384 dims. Also ask them to stop retries and re-run repro with `--no-retry` flag.

Alex (support): replied to customer with repro steps: 1) run this curl to reproduce and send us response headers + request id, 2) show sdk config (model alias + batch_size + retry policy), 3) timeframe of failing requests (we have traces).

Customer (via paste into thread): they ran quick test and got `200` with 384 dims using `embed-small-legacy` then got 422 when their ingestion validated dims. They confirmed their client retried 3x on 5xx by default.

SRE-bot: detected deploy `eng-runtime v1.48.2` at 07:00 UTC then a config change to batching defaults at 07:03 UTC on canary. No rollback.

Chris (eng-runtime): to mitigate: 1) pin routing for ACME to `embed-large-v2` if they need 1536 dims, or 2) create a transient alias that maps `embed-small-legacy` -> `embed-large-v2` (not ideal). Also added a quick fix to route malformed `Content-Length` requests into a fast-fail path rather than fallback slow-path — will push a patch to canary.

Maria (observability): for future, we should surface per-request `batching_hold_ms` in the per-request breakdown in the embedding dashboard (currently it's buried in traces). I'll add a small dashboard tile and an alert when average batching_hold_ms > 250ms for a route.

Jordan (billing): asked support to hold off on credit until we confirm retries and duplication. If confirmed, perform proportional credit. Also suggest we add a billing-dedupe window for identical request ids within 60s for high-retry cases (needs product approval).

Priya (support-l2): next steps assigned: Alex to collect full headers + sample request-id(s); Maria to add dashboard tile and snapshot; Chris to push canary patch to short-circuit fallback; Jordan to run billing impact calc; customer asked for guidance on how to avoid future spikes.

Alex (support): collected headers and full trace links from customer; attached sanitized headers and trace ids in the ticket. Also asked them to run repro with `--no-retry` and confirm billing trend.

Customer (short): "we moved back to embed-large-v2 and cost normalized. Thanks!" :tada:

Chris (eng-runtime): patch merged to canary — new behavior: malformed content-length yields 400 with clear error `invalid content-length` instead of slow fallback. Rolling to stable in 2h if canary metrics look good.

Maria (observability): added dashboard tile and set alert threshold. Shared permalink in thread.

Jordan (billing): provisional credit prepared pending final verification; will finalize after 24h of normalized traffic.

Priya (support-l2): closing loop with customer: summary + best-practices: 1) ensure model alias matches expected vector dim, 2) avoid aggressive retry policies for 5xx on embeddings (use exponential backoff + idempotency keys), 3) verify SDK batch_size and Content-Encoding headers.

Alex (support): marking resolved once billing is finalized. Leaving thread open for 48h.

Chris (eng-runtime): FYI — follow-up action item to add a machine-readable `expected_dim` to model descriptors in the catalog so SDKs can warn at client-time. Filed RFC: RFD-embed-dim-hints.

Priya (support-l2): thanks everyone — nice quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
